coverage_summary: All 60 model-visible files were listed; none were excluded as binary/sensitive per get_source_scope (excluded_over_5_mib=0, excluded_sensitive_name_or_path=0, excluded_symlinks=0). I fully read the primary security-relevant files: Cleaner.java, Whitelist.java, Entities.java, Attribute.java, Attributes.java, DataNode.java, DataUtil.java, StringUtil.java, plus Node.absUrl and Cleaner-relevant parts of Node.java and HtmlTreeBuilder.java. I partially inspected the large parser state machines (Tokeniser.java, TokeniserState.java, HtmlTreeBuilderState.java) around raw-text/RCDATA transitions and Cleaner/DataNode creation, and searched for DataNode creation, absUrl use, and protocol validation. I did not read every line of HtmlTreeBuilderState.java (71 KB), TokeniserState.java (61 KB), Element.java (44 KB), HttpConnection.java (34 KB), or the example/select/helper files in full; network request construction/redirect handling and the full tree-construction state matrix are the main uninspected areas.
limitations: No test files, changelog, git history, or patch data are present in the snapshot, so version-to-fix comparison was impossible; the 1.8.3-SNAPSHOT label alone is not evidence of a specific flaw.
No execution, instrumentation, or dependency/OSV data was used (prohibited); all conclusions are static-source-level and none are runtime-confirmed.

The two largest parser files (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java, TokeniserState.java) and HttpConnection.java were only partially inspected; a parser-differential sanitizer bypass or network-layer issue in the unread portions cannot be excluded.
Attacker-control assessment assumes the standard use of Jsoup.clean/Jsoup.isValid on untrusted HTML fragments; application-specific whitelists could change reachability of the rejected leads.

rejected_leads.lead: Cleaner copies DataNode content unescaped (Cleaner.java:103-106; DataNode.outerHtmlHead emits getWholeData() raw, DataNode.java:42-44) when the DataNode's parent is a whitelist-safe tag.
rejected_leads.reason: Parser only creates DataNodes under `script`/`style` (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:230-237), neither of which is in any default whitelist. Exploitation requires an application whitelist that explicitly allows script/style (explicit misconfiguration); for unsafe parents the DataNode is counted as discarded and not emitted. No attacker-controlled path to a safe DataNode parent was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Whitelist.testValidProtocol (Whitelist.java:514-541) relies on Node.absUrl (Node.java:178-203); when URL resolution fails it falls back to the raw attribute value and does a case-insensitive startsWith check against allowed protocol prefixes.
rejected_leads.reason: The fallback value must still literally start with an allowed prefix (e.g. `http:`), and java.net.URL throws on unknown schemes such as `javascript:`, so the raw value is then rejected. Schemes mis-encoded with control characters/entities fail the prefix check and are removed (fail-closed). No source-supported input that passes the prefix check and is executed as script by a browser was identified.

rejected_leads.lead: Whitelist.removeAttributes(':all', ...) mutates the `attributes` map while iterating `attributes.keySet()` (Whitelist.java:306-313), which can throw ConcurrentModificationException.
rejected_leads.reason: Real code defect, but reachable only by the embedding application calling removeAttributes with ':all'; it is not reached by parsing/cleaning attacker HTML and has no confidentiality/integrity impact, so it is not a submission-grade security finding.

rejected_leads.lead: In-attribute escaping leaves `<` and `>` unescaped (Entities.escape, Entities.java:120-131, called from Attribute.html:82-89).
rejected_leads.reason: Attribute values are always emitted inside double quotes and `&` and `"` are escaped, so the unescaped angle brackets cannot break out of the attribute context; no mXSS/serialization bypass demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: Snapshot version 1.8.3-SNAPSHOT is contemporaneous with historically reported Cleaner/XSS issues in jsoup 1.8.x.
rejected_leads.reason: I could not localize a concrete vulnerable code path from the source alone; without an external patch/advisory comparison (not permitted in this run) this remains an unconfirmed lead, not evidence-backed.

rejected_leads.lead: Potential parser-differential / mXSS behavior around raw-text and RCDATA elements (noscript, xmp, iframe, noembed, noframes, plaintext) in Tokeniser/TokeniserState.
rejected_leads.reason: Raw-text content is turned into text/data under the raw element itself; the default whitelists do not allow those tags, and text nodes are re-escaped on output. No allowed element was found that causes browser re-parsing to produce executable markup.

summary: Reviewed the assigned jsoup snapshot (pom.xml declares 1.8.3-SNAPSHOT; 60 main-source files, no test/resource fixtures beyond entity properties). I focused on the security-relevant trust boundary of this library: the HTML parser feeding the whitelist-based `Cleaner`/`Whitelist` sanitizer, plus attribute URL handling, entity/attribute escaping, and the render/URL-resolution helpers. I traced attacker-controlled markup through Tokeniser -> HtmlTreeBuilder -> Cleaner, and checked the protocol/attribute validation logic for bypasses. I could not substantiate a concrete, exploitable vulnerability with the required source evidence: the sanitizer's raw-data (script/style) copy path is gated on a whitelist that explicitly allows the raw tag, URL protocol checks are prefix checks over `absUrl` output with a raw-value fallback that still must match an explicitly allowed protocol prefix, and attribute serialization quotes values and escapes `"`/`&`. I am therefore submitting no candidate rather than inventing one. Key unconfirmed leads are recorded below.
